structure.rationale: The requester's 22-chapter syllabus is kept intact and in order: Part I frames the problem (files vs tables, platform history, what Iceberg is and is not); Part II builds the core model (three layers, snapshots, schema, partitioning, row-level change); Part III covers architecture and design principles (catalog, storage, openness, reliability, governance); Part IV applies them to use cases; Part V turns them into decisions. Each chapter follows the requester's shape: problem scene, concept, how it works (visual), design principle, use case, decision guidance.
structure.audience: Data engineers, analytics engineers, architects, technical leaders, and product managers who need to reason about lakehouse architecture, not run Iceberg commands.
structure.voice: thing-explainer: common words, one scene per chapter, technical terms introduced once in quotes.
